prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
The blog is built and running, and every page I checked returned 200 with no block-render failures.

**View it** at https://localhost:44317/ (HTTP: http://localhost:41576). It's running now from `dotnet run` in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco`. The backoffice login is `admin@example.com` / `1234567890`.

**What I built**
- **Modeling (MCP):**
  - Five block types in the Blocks folder: `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock` and `blogPostListBlock`.
  - Two block grid data types, "Blog Front Page Blocks" and "Blog Post Blocks".
  - Two page types in the Pages folder, `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost`, each with a template.
  - I edited the scaffold's `siteRoot` type so the front page can sit under WWW.
- **Content (MCP):**
  - A published "The MCP Blog" front page under WWW, with the domain `/`. Its grid has a hero block and a "Latest posts" list block.
  - Two published posts about why MCP is awesome. Each has a hero image and a grid of rich text, image and quote blocks.
  - Six Unsplash photos imported into a "Blog" media folder, with photographer credits in the captions.
- **Razor (after the rebuild):**
  - Pages render with `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`.
  - Each block has an adapter in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml`, a plain model in `Models/Blocks/`, a ViewComponent in `ViewComponents/`, and its markup in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
  - There are also a shared `_Layout`, a `PostHeader` ViewComponent for the post header, and a few rich-text styles added to `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css`.
  - I ran `npm install` and `npm run build`, which writes `wwwroot/dist/site.css`. All images go through `GetCropUrl`.

**Checks:** both posts, all five image URLs and the CSS return 200. The front page lists both posts, newest first.

**Things to know**
- Nothing is broken that I found. I only inspected the HTML and requests, not the pages in a browser, so the visual styling is untested.
- The `Views/_ViewImports.cshtml` default pointed at `Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common.PublishedModels`, but the generated models are in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models`. I changed the import.
- The post list adapter reads the current page from `UmbracoContext` rather than a friendly extension. That is the one place I wasn't sure of the convention.
- `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` in `.mcp.json` is the scaffold's own setting for the dev certificate. I left it alone.
